statements.impact_statement: OpenSSH host key handling use-after-free. The restic image carries the ssh client binaries (openssh-client-common, openssh-client-default and openssh-keygen 10.3_p1-r0) in its Alpine layer. Nothing that runs the image starts ssh: restic runs it for an sftp: repository (observed), and all nine workloads (the database, OpenBao and etcd backup CronJobs, the two restore tests, the dump load test, the backup verifier and the two audit-sink shippers) build their repository URL with a fixed `s3:` prefix (in the script, or in the ExternalSecret template for the shippers); none of their scripts calls ssh, sftp, scp or ssh-keygen.
statements.action_statement: Re-check on restic 0.19.2 (0.19.1, built 2026-07-05, is still the newest tag on GitHub and Docker Hub on 2026-11-10; no rebuilt tag exists: Alpine has OpenSSH 10.3_p1-r1, the image still carries 10.3_p1-r0, three CRITICAL rows, all CVE-2026-60002, local Trivy 0.69.3). Drop this statement once a fixed tag is pinned. Re-read at once if a script ever uses an sftp: or rclone: repository or runs ssh.
statements.status_notes: Expires: 2027-01-09. Renewed 2026-11-10 (first recorded 2026-10-22, renewed 2026-11-04). Re-read on 2026-11-10 at the apps 0.4.5 candidate: the same nine manifests carry the image line (databases, openbao and etcd backup, both restore tests, dump-load-test with restic-dump.sh, backup-verify with restic-stage.sh, both audit-sink shippers with ship.sh); every repository URL is built with the `s3:` prefix (RESTIC_REPOSITORY in the scripts, RESTIC_REPO_BASE in the two shipper ExternalSecrets); a search of apps/base/backup and of both audit-sink bricks for ssh, sftp, scp, ssh-keygen and rclone finds no call. The run of 2026-11-04 in the image against a fake S3 store with failing ssh stand-ins (0 calls; the same image on an sftp: repository calls ssh at once) was not repeated. No cluster was used.
